gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both concern the abstract meta-theorem, but ISSUE-001 diagnoses an unstated separability requirement for constructing finite-dimensional dictionaries. Gold I001 diagnoses a mismatch between strict-sublevel grid approximations and the claimed closed target, with a different target-identification obligation.

Gold I002 concerns failure of threshold membership stabilization under numerical convergence in the finite-grid construction. ISSUE-002 concerns noncompact L1 unit spheres and failure of the F2 quadrature lemma under nonsupported measures, a separate analytic defect.

Both identify that without full support, nonzero functions can have zero L1 norm, so the claimed norm equivalence and compactness of the L1 unit sphere in the uniform norm fail; the quadrature conclusion and F2 justification therefore do not follow.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The F2 proof incorrectly treats the L1 seminorm as a norm on an arbitrary finite-dimensional function space when the measure has a nontrivial null direction, invalidating compactness and the uniform quadrature estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: Failure of compactness and of the universal F2 quadrature conclusion because an L1-null nonzero direction exists when the measure lacks full support.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 gives the same unsupported-measure counterexample, explains the null direction and noncompact unit sphere, states the resulting quadrature failure, and supplies the quotient/full-support repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both affect a Borel-measurability argument, but I004 concerns the impossible existence of a universal pointwise Borel evaluator and the resulting projection construction. ISSUE-005 concerns an incorrect neighborhood-ball identity in a pointwise-limit lemma; its standard repair does not recognize the evaluator impossibility.

Both identify that the greedy star-priority recursion can terminate even when the input tree contains a Silver witness with unboundedly many free coordinates. The resulting bounded periods break the claimed Silver-tree spectral equivalence and its hardness consequences.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The greedy local admissibility rule is not extension-preserving: it can select a prefix that later dies despite an existing coherent Silver witness, so the selected star counts do not certify the witness and the spectral equivalence fails.

component_coverage.gold_component: The greedy recursion can die on a tree containing a Silver tree, invalidating the claimed maximality and the forward spectral implication.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 supplies an explicit tree counterexample, shows the greedy sequence reaches bottom despite a Silver subtree, derives bounded periods and failure of the non-torsion spectral implication, and explains that a coherent-witness construction is required.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the recursion may output bottom although the odometer is defined only for ordinary ternary patterns, making the map undefined on part of its declared domain and leaving the dependent regularity and spectral claims unsupported.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The construction has no defined odometer/map value on the bottom failure branch, so F_S and Ψ(S) are not total on all trees until an explicit convention is added.

component_coverage.gold_component: Undefined map construction on the bottom branch and consequent failure of all-tree regularity and spectral claims.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly identifies bottom outputs, the domain mismatch, the resulting undefined F_S and Ψ(S), the affected claims, and a concrete bottom-branch convention.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid inference from approximate eigenvectors or small lower norms along varying countable blocks to membership in the closure of the union of block approximate spectra. The supplied repair in ISSUE-006 adds the needed uniform transfer estimate and handles the specialized finite-order dynamics.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: For countably many blocks, lower norms tending to zero along changing blocks do not by themselves imply the global approximate point spectrum equals the closure of the union of block approximate spectra; a uniform blockwise resolvent/transfer argument is required.

component_coverage.gold_component: Failure of the general countable-block spectral union equality because varying-block approximate eigenvectors do not establish the reverse inclusion without a uniform transfer estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 directly attacks the same varying-block inference, explains why small lower norms are insufficient, identifies the affected countable-block uses, and proposes the uniform finite-order resolvent restriction or proof needed to recover the formula.
